title: Shape Hierarchy Project
instructions: Implement the `Shape`, `Circle`, and `Rectangle` classes according to the requirements, ensuring correct use of inheritance, `super()`, method overriding, and then demonstrate polymorphism.
steps: Complete the base class `Shape` with `__init__(name)` and placeholder methods `area()` and `perimeter()`.
Complete the `Circle` class, using `super()` to handle the `name` attribute and overriding `area()` and `perimeter()` to calculate the correct values.
Complete the `Rectangle` class, using `super()` to handle the `name` attribute and overriding `area()` and `perimeter()` to calculate the correct values.
Instantiate a `Circle` (radius 5, name 'My Circle') and a `Rectangle` (width 10, height 5, name 'My Rectangle').
Define the function `calculate_and_display(shapes_list)` to call the `area()` and `perimeter()` methods on all shapes in the list.
Call `calculate_and_display` with a list containing both instances.
hints: In `Circle.__init__` and `Rectangle.__init__`, the call should be `super().__init__(name)`.
Ensure the overridden methods return a numeric value so they can be formatted with `:.2f` in the output.
Polymorphism works because the `calculate_and_display` function only expects objects to have `area()` and `perimeter()` methods.
